_: Mutants for scripts/mutate.py. Each is a plausible mistake, not a nonsense edit: the question is whether the suite would catch a change somebody might actually make. Run with `python scripts/mutate.py`.

not_mutated.name: the isfinite guard in splat
not_mutated.why: removing it is undefined behaviour ((int)floor(NaN)), not a wrong answer - on x86 the garbage index lands out of bounds and the picture is identical, so no test can kill it. It stays because UB is not a thing to leave in.

mutants.name: the hull is never popped (brute force would still be right)
a downhill horizon is reported instead of clamped to flat
line offsets truncate instead of rounding
distance along the ray ignores the direction's obliqueness
heights scale with the cell, not the tile
the line is read forwards whichever way the ray points
mutants.find: const int a = step > 0 ? a_first + k : a_last - k;

not_mutated.name: the tangent pop's <= could be <
not_mutated.why: output-equivalent, not untested. The two differ only when two hull candidates have exactly equal slope, and then both report the same value; the strict form just keeps the collinear point on the stack. The brute-force battery includes a pure ramp, which is collinear end to end, and it agrees under both.
